_what: Undervoltage rungs a card can be asked to sit at, ported from the host script ops/scripts/gpu-undervolt. A plan belongs to a *card*, not to a configuration: it outlives a switch, and it outlives nothing else -- these are volatile driver settings and a reboot returns a card to stock on its own, which is the recovery method and is deliberately not replaced by anything here. Which card runs which plan is operational state (`.state/host.json`, `power_plans`); the numbers, the rung names, the envelope and the evidence are source, because they are what the runtime validates and renders. Cards nobody has measured have no plan and are refused a rung rather than being handed another card's numbers.

envelope._why: 15 MHz is the driver's granularity, so a value off the step is rounded rather than refused. +150 MHz is the envelope proven on this driver family (+15..+150 accepted and held); a held +300 faulted a live serving context with Xid 31, and API acceptance is not serving safety. The clock floor stays at 210 MHz: a high floor is what makes an offsetting card crash at idle.

rtx3090.measured: 2026-10-18: -12.5% energy per token, identical output. Evidence, ladder and gates: ops/reports/2026-10-18-rtx3090-undervolt/

rtx3080-ti.measured: 2026-10-18: -11.8% energy per token, identical output. rtx4080-super.name: RTX 4080 SUPER (AD103)
rtx4080-super.measured: 2026-10-19 ladder: sensible -16% energy per token (prefill windows; -32% clean decode window), identical output; assertive failed the >=98% pooled-decode gate in two windows. First Ada card through the ladder: no Ampere number survived translation. Evidence: ops/reports/2026-10-19-4080super-undervolt/summary.md
rtx4080-super.note: The default here is `safe`, one rung toward stock from the ladder winner, and that is not a measurement result: running `sensible` in daytime service the LLM simply stopped (owner-reported 2026-10-20, from live use). Recorded as reported, not corroborated -- the engine's own log starts after the move, with no Xid or OOM line inside what survived. What `sensible` failed is the production duty cycle, not the bench gates, so it stays in the table as a measured rung and `safe` is what a one-click apply means.

rtx2080-ti.name: RTX 2080 Ti (TU102)
rtx2080-ti.measured: 2026-10-27: measured for efficiency on 2026-10-26 and re-qualified for function on 2026-10-27, on two RTX 2080 Ti FE boards that hold one Strata model between them, so every rung is applied to both and sampled on both. Efficiency (2026-10-26 campaign): sensible, as it stands now at 220 W / +105, measured -8.91% joules per token with identical answers; the same 220 W cap at +60 measured -9.19% - the saving lives in the cap, not in the offset. Function (2026-10-27): a rung ships only after four four-minute phases with both halves pinned at their power cap, plus four engine profile switches including a cross-model one, with the kernel log as the authority. At +150 an ordinary short request faults card a with Xid 31 in about 40 seconds, cold. At +105 requests and cold switches pass and the card faults about 15 minutes into sustained load (Xid 13 at 20:53:50, Xid 31 at 20:55:37 UTC). At +60 and +75 on 220 W, and at 260 W, the protocol passes with no Xid and identical answers; offset 0 passes the same 31 minutes, so neither heat nor switching alone faults this board. Card a runs 5-7 C hotter than card b at lower draw in every paired sample, and every fault in the record is on card a. Money for the shipped sensible (220 W, +60): 32.6 W saved while loaded, idle penalty +1.02 W and +0.35 W on cards a and b, break-even just over 1 loaded hour a day, -239 Wh/day at 8 h/day (about $9.26/yr at 0.10613 USD/kWh). Campaigns: /home/astigmatism/ops/reports/2026-10-26-2080ti-undervolt/ and /home/astigmatism/ops/reports/2026-10-27-rung-requalification/.
rtx2080-ti.note: No rung on this board carries a clock cap, and none may silently acquire one. The campaign measured power and offset with the driver's clock lock deleted after every window (instrument/measure.sh: drop_lock), because a positive V/F offset makes this board ask for clocks *above* its nominal top bin — at +150 a card ran 2175 MHz — so `-lgc 210,2160` is a real cap at exactly these offsets rather than a no-op. Whether a cap below the top bin is merely harmful or catastrophic is still open: the lock sweep (03:22-03:30) showed `-lgc` does hold and is invisible in `clocks.max.sm`, but its 30-second windows never left the ramp, and the earlier figure of a lost 82 % of decode turned out to be a log-parsing artifact. What is settled is the shipping shape: every long-window number here was taken unlocked, so a Turing rung states `clock_max: null` and the write drops the lock. The runtime already does the right thing with a null (runtime/gpucard.py:182 falls to -rgc, runtime/power.py:192 omits --clock-max); only the registry validator had to learn that null is an intention. The default sits on the rung the campaign recommends; a reboot returns both cards to stock by itself, which is the recovery method. Re-qualified 2026-10-27 for function, not just efficiency: every rung here has been driven through long sessions and hot engine profile switches on the machine's own controller, and the rung that was here before was not. See /home/astigmatism/reports/2026-10-27-rung-requalification/.
